correctness.rationale: Checked the full horizontal-section proof. A shear/scale can center both positive parallel bases and turn their half-widths into 1 and t while keeping the normalized area ratio. Put β=λ/(1+λ). For λ<1 the bottom sections of the two bottom copies are disjoint, and no top copy meets the bottom. For β≥1/2 the top pair covers every section y≥1−β (its halfwidth is at least tβ≥t(1−β)). Below that height only the bottom pair is available, with halfwidth β−(1−t)y around the centers ±(1−β), so the entire gap for t<1 is y_0<y<1−β, |x|<(1−t)(y−y_0), y_0=(2β−1)/(1−t). Its height is positive iff λ<2−t, and integration gives (1−t)(1−β−y_0)^2. Dividing by 1+t gives the stated deficit including the zero at critical equality; the quadratic coefficient and λ=1 value follow. For t=1 the overlapping height ranges of the two pairs cover the whole parallelogram at β≥1/2 without dividing by 1−t. RESULT.md and both supplementary files were inspected. The expected 39,919 verifier count is not a recorded replay; the rational grid and algebraic consistency checks cannot prove the real-parameter theorem.

Taking F>λ gives x+y>λ−t, x<ty+1−tλ, y<tx+1−tλ. The three intersections are (a,a), (λ−1,1−t), and (1−t,λ−1), with a=(1−λt)/(1−t).
